questions.q: A charge of $4\muC$ is to be divided into two. The distance between the two divided charges is constant. The magnitude of the divided charges so that the force between them is maximum, will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If after division, one of the charge is& $q$~the other charge will be~ \left(4 - q\right)$. The force between them can be written as,

$F = \dfrac{Kq\left(4 - q\right)}{d2}$

For the force between them to be maximum,

$\dfrac{dF}{dq} = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{K}{d2}\left[4 - 2q\right] = 0$

$⇒ q = 2\mu C$

$

questions.q: Considering a group of positive charges, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Net potential of the system cannot be zero at a point but net electric field can be zero at that point
Net potential of the system at a point can be zero but net electric field can't be zero at that point
Both the net potential and the net field can be zero at a point
Both the net potential and the net electric field cannot be zero at a point
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, net potential will be algebraic sum of potential due to each charge, so we can write& ${V}_{net} = ∑ \left(\dfrac{k{Q}_{i}}{ri}\right).

As given in the question,~${Q}_{i}$~and~${r}_{i}$ are positive, so

$∴ {V}_{net} > 0$

But electric field is a vector quantity, so it can be zero for a given arrangement of charges. For example, electric field at the centre of the two equal charges at certain distance will be zero as electric field due to both charges will be in opposite direction and hence will cancel each other.

$

questions.q: The electrostatic potential on the surface of uniformly charged spherical shell of radius $\mathrm{R}=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ is 120 V. The potential at the centre of shell, at a distance $\mathrm{r}=5 \mathrm{~cm}$ from centre, and at a distance $\mathrm{r}=15 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the centre of the shell respectively, are :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Potential inside shell is equal to potential on surface
$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathrm{V}_{\text {surface }}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}}{\mathrm{R}}=120 \mathrm{~V}$
at $\mathrm{r}=15 \mathrm{~cm}$
$\mathrm{V}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}}{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{120 \times 10}{15}=80 \mathrm{~V}$

questions.q: A positive point charge is released from rest at a distance ${r}_{0}$ from a positive line charge with uniform charge density. The speed $( v )$ of the point charge, as a function of instantaneous distance $r$ from line charge, is proportional to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} = q ∆ V$
$\dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} = q \times \dfrac{λ}{2{πε}_{0}} \left(ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{r}{r0}\right)\right)
$v^{2} = $\dfrac{qλ}{m \pi ε0} \left(ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{r}{r0}\right)\right)
$v = $\sqrt{\dfrac{qλ}{m \pi ε0}\left(ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{r}{r0}\right)\right)}

$v ∝ \sqrt{ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{r}{r0}\right)}$

$

questions.q:
A charge Q is distributed over two concentric conducting thin spherical shells radii& $r$ and~$R \left(R > r\right). If the surface charge densities on the two shells are equal, the electric potential at the common centre is :&

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${Q}_{1} = \sigma4{πr}^{2}$

${Q}_{2} = \sigma4{πr}^{2}$

$\begin{cases}∴ & Q = \sigma4\pi\left(r^{2} + R^{2}\right) \\ ∴ & \sigma = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi\left(r^{2} + R^{2}\right)}\end{cases}$

${V}_{C} = \dfrac{KQ1}{r} + \dfrac{KQ2}{R}$

questions.q:
A particle of charge $- q$ and mass $m$ moves in a circle of radius $r$ around an infinitely long line charge of linear density $+ \lambda$. Then time period will be given as:
(Consider $k$ as Coulomb's constant)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Attractive electrostatic force due to line charge on the charged particle will provide the required centripetal force. Therefore,

$q\left(\dfrac{2k\lambda}{r}\right) = m{ω}^{2}r$

$⇒ {ω}^{2} = \dfrac{2k\lambdaq}{mr^{2}}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)2 = \dfrac{2k\lambdaq}{mr^{2}}$

$⇒ T = 2\pir\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2k\lambdaq}}$

questions.q:
A system of three charges are placed as shown in the figure:

If $D > > d,$ the potential energy of the system is best given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$U = \dfrac{k\left(- q\right)\left(q\right)}{d} + \dfrac{k\left(- q\right)\left(Q\right)}{\left(\dfrac{d}{2} - D\right)} + \dfrac{k\left(q\right)\left(Q\right)}{\left(D + \dfrac{d}{2}\right)}$
$= \dfrac{- kq^{2}}{d} - \dfrac{kQq}{\left(D - \dfrac{d}{2}\right)} + \dfrac{KQq}{\left(D + \dfrac{d}{2}\right)}$
$= \dfrac{- kq^{2}}{d} + kQq \left(\dfrac{- D - \dfrac{d}{2} + D - \dfrac{d}{2}}{D^{2} - \dfrac{d^{2}}{4}}\right)
$= $\dfrac{- kq^{2}}{d} - \dfrac{kQqd}{D^{2} - \dfrac{d^{2}}{4}}
Since, D>>d
$U = $\dfrac{- kq^{2}}{d} - \dfrac{kQqd}{D^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}} \left[- \dfrac{q^{2}}{d} - \dfrac{qQd}{D^{2}}\right]$

questions.q: A $10\muC$~charge is divided into two parts and placed at $1$ cm distance so that the repulsive force between them is maximum. The charges of the two parts are:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the charges be& $x\mu C, \left(q - x\right)\mu C$, where~$q = 10\mu C$

The force between them is~

$F = \dfrac{Kx ( q - x )}{r2}$.

For the force to be maximum,

$\dfrac{dF}{dx} = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{dF}{dx} = \dfrac{K ( q - 2x )}{r2} = 0 ⇒ x = \dfrac{q}{2} = 5\mu C$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ has an initial velocity $\overset{→}{v} = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j}$ . If an electric field $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}$ and magnetic field $\overset{→}{B} = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{i}$& act on the particle, its speed will double after a time
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration produced by electric field,
$a = \dfrac{q{E}_{0}}{m}\overset{^}{i}$

After time $t$, velocity of the particle,
$v = u + at$

$⇒ v = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j} + \left(\dfrac{q{E}_{0}t}{m}\right)\overset{^}{i}\left[$∵ u = v = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j}\right]$

So, speed of the particle,
\left|v\right| = $\sqrt{{v}_{0}^{2} + \left(\dfrac{q{E}_{0}t}{m}\right)2}

Now, given \left|v\right| = 2{v}_{0}$after time $t$, so
$2{v}_{0} = $\sqrt{{v}_{0}^{2} + $\$left(\dfrac{q{E}_{0}t}{m}\right)$2}

$⇒ 4{v}_{0}^{2} = {v}_{0}^{2} + \$left(\dfrac{q{E}_{0}t}{m}\right)$2$

$⇒ 3{v}_{0}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{q{E}_{0}t}{m}\right)2$

So, time interval, $t = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}m{v}_{0}}{q{E}_{0}}

Here, we must note that no change in magnitude of velocity is caused by a perpendicular magnetic field. So, we are not taking effect of magnetic field while calculating change in speed.

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason $\mathrm{R}$ Assertion A : Work done in moving a test charge between two points inside a uniformly charged spherical shell is zero, no matter which path is chosen.
Reason $\mathrm{R}$ : Electrostatic potential inside a uniformly charged spherical shell is constant and is same as that on the surface of the shell. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true and $\mathrm{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$
Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true but $\mathrm{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a uniformly charged spherical shell:
- The electric field inside the shell is zero everywhere (from Gauss's law)
* When the electric field is zero, no work is done in moving a charge
- Since work - force $\times$displacement, and force - q̧E (where E - 0), work - 0
- The potential inside is constant and equal to the value at the surface
Assertion A is correct: Since the electric field is zero everywhere inside the shell, no work is done moving a charge between any two points, regardless of path.
Reason R is correct: The potential inside a uniformly charged spherical shell is indeed constant and equal to the value at the surface.
Does R explain $A$ ? Yes, because:
- Constant potential means zero electric field (since $\mathrm{E}=-\mathrm{FW}$)
- Zero electric field means no force on a test charge
- No force means no work done in moving the charge
Therefore, opxion (2) is correct: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: Two identical charged particles each having a mass $10g$ and charge $2 . 0 \times {10}^{- 7}C$ are placed on a horizontal table with a separation of $L$ between them such that they stay in limited equilibrium. If the coefficient of friction between each particle and the table is $0 . 25$, find the value of $L$. [Use $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Normal reaction applied by table& on object will be,& $N = mg$.

Both charges are same, hence a repulsive force will act between them.

Value of force acting will be,~$\dfrac{kQ^{2}}{L2}$.

Now the maximum value of friction force which table can provide is,

$= \muN = \mumg$

For equilibrium,~$\dfrac{kQ^{2}}{L2} = \mumg$.

$L = \sqrt{\dfrac{kQ^{2}}{\mumg}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{0 . 25mg}}Q = 2\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{mg}}Q$

$= 2\sqrt{\dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9}}{10 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 10}}\left(2 \times {10}^{- 7}\right) = 0 . 12m = 12cm$

questions.q:
Charges $- q$ and $+ q$, located at $A$ and $B$, respectively, constitute an electric dipole. Distance $AB = 2a$,~$O$ is the mid point of the dipole and $OP$ is perpendicular to $AB$. A charge $Q$ is placed at $P$ where $OP = y$ and $y ≫ 2a$. The charge $Q$ experiences an electrostatic force $F$. If $Q$ is now moved along the equatorial line to $P '$ such that $OP ' = \left(\dfrac{y}{3}\right)$the force on $Q$ will be close $to $\$left(\dfrac{y}{3}≪ 2a\right)$
$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric field intensity at the distance $y$~along the perpendicular bisector is

\left|{E}_{1}\right| = \dfrac{KP}{y3}$

So, force at distance $y$ on~$Q$,

$F = Q ( {E}_{1} ) = Q \left(\dfrac{KP}{y3}\right) ...($1 )$

$F ' = $Q\dfrac{KP}{ \left(\dfrac{y}{3}\right)$3}$ ...( 2 )$

Dividing~ \left($1\right)$~by~ \left(2\right)$, we get,

$\dfrac{F '}{F} = \left(3\right)3$

$∴ F ' = 27F$

$

questions.q:
Two electrons each are fixed at a distance $2d .$~A third charge proton placed at the midpoint is displaced slightly by a distance $x \left(x ≪ d\right)$ perpendicular to the line joining the two fixed charges. Proton will execute simple harmonic motion having angular frequency:
($m = mass of charged particle)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the given condition, we have

${F}_{netq} = - \left[$2{F}_{q / q}cos$\theta\right]

${F}_{netq} = - 2 $\cdot \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \cdot \dfrac{q2}{\left(\sqrt{d^{2} + x^{2}}\right)2} \cdot \dfrac{x}{d^{2} + x^{2}}

$= - $\dfrac{q2}{2\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{x}{\left(d^{2} + x^{2}\right)3 / 2}

For~$x < < d,$

${F}_{netq} = - \dfrac{q2}{2\pi{ε}_{0}d^{3}}x$

$∴ a = - \dfrac{q2}{2\pi{ε}_{0} \cdot md^{3}}x$

Comparing with equation of SHM~ \left(a = - {ω}^{2}x\right)$

$∴ \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{q2}{2\pi{ε}_{0}md^{3}}}

$

questions.q: Three infinitely long wires with linear charge density $\lambda$ are placed along the $x-a x i s, y$-axis and $z-$ axis respectively. Which of the following denotes an equipotential surface?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Potential due to an infinite wire is $V=2 k \lambda \ln r$, where $r$ is the distance from the wire. Taking the point in space $P(x, y, z)$
Distance from wire along $x$-axis is $r_x=\sqrt{y^2+z^2}$
Distance from wire along $y$-axis is $r_y=\sqrt{x^2+z^2}$
Distance from wire along $z$-axis is $r_z=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\Rightarrow$ Potential at $P$ due to wire along $x$-axis is
$V_x=2 k \lambda \ln r_x$ Potential at $P$ due to wire along $y$-axis is
$V_y=2 k \lambda \ln r_y$ Potential at $P$ due to wire along $z$-axis is
$V_z=2 k \lambda \ln r_z\Rightarrow$ Not potential at $P=V=V_x+V_y+V_z$
or $\quad V=2 k \lambda \ln r_x+2 k \lambda \ln r_y+2 k \lambda \ln r_z$
i.e. $V=2 k \lambda \ln  \left(r_x r_y r_z\right)$
or
\begin{aligned}$& V=2 k \lambda \ln \left(\sqrt{y^2+z²} \sqrt{z^2+x²} \sqrt{x^2+y²}\right)\\ \text{ and } =k \lambda \ln \left(y^2+z²\$right)\left($z^2+x²\right)\left(x²+y²\right)
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow$ For equipotential surface
\left(x²+y²\$right)\left($y^2+z²\right)\left(z^2+x²\right)=\text { constant }$

questions.q:
The three charges $\dfrac{q}{2}, q$~and $\dfrac{q}{2}$~are placed at the corners $A, D$ and $C$ of a square of side $a$~as shown in figure. The magnitude of electric field \left(E\right)$~at the corner $B$ of the square, is&

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${E}_{A} = \dfrac{k\left(\dfrac{q}{2}\right)}{a2} = \dfrac{kq}{2a^{2}}$,~ ${E}_{C} = \dfrac{k\left(\dfrac{q}{2}\right)}{a2} = \dfrac{kq}{2a^{2}}$~ and ${E}_{D} = \dfrac{k\left(q\right)}{\left(\sqrt{2}a\right)2} = \dfrac{kq}{2a^{2}}$

As we can see from diagram,~${E}_{C} \text{ and } {E}_{A}$~are perpendicular.

Therefore, net electric field will be,

$= \dfrac{kq}{2a^{2}} + \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{kq}{2a^{2}}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{kq}{2a^{2}}\right)2} = \dfrac{kq}{2a^{2}} + \dfrac{kq}{\sqrt{2}a^{2}} = \dfrac{q}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}a^{2}} \left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$

questions.q: Two identical positive charges $Q$ each are fixed at a distance of $2a$~apart from each other. Another point charge ${q}_{0}$ with mass $m$~is placed at midpoint between two fixed charges. For a small displacement along the line joining the fixed charges, the charge ${q}_{0}$ executes SHM. The time period of oscillation of charge ${q}_{0}$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the charged particle be displaced slightly towards right by distance $x \left(x ≪ d\right)$.

\left(QatA, q\right): {F}_{1} = $\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{Qq}{\left(d + x\right)2},towards right

\l$left(Q\text{at}$B, q\right): {F}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{Qq}{\left(d - x\right)2},$towards left

$\overset{→}{F}net = \overset{→}{F}1 + \overset{→}{F}2$, will bring it towards $O$.$\overset{→}{F}net = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}}\left[\dfrac{1}{\left(d + x\right)2} - \dfrac{1}{\left(d - x\right)2}\right]\overset{^}{i}$

$= \dfrac{- Qq}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}}\left[\dfrac{4xd}{\left(d^{2} - x^{2}\right)2}\right]\overset{^}{i}$

Since $x ≪ d, x^{2}$ is negligible.

$\overset{→}{F}net = - \left(\dfrac{Qq}{\pi{ϵ}_{0}d^{3}}\right) \timesx\overset{^}{i}

Clearly, the direction of the force is opposite to the displacement &~$F ∝ x$, hence it is an SHM.

Acceleration of charged particle is given as,

$a = $\dfrac{F}{m} = - \dfrac{Qq}{\pi{ϵ}_{0}md^{3}}$x . . . . \left($1\right)$

And we know that for SHM,

$a = - {ω}^{2}x \ldots . \left($2\right)$

Comparing \left(1\right)$~and \left(2\right)$, we get

$\omega = $\sqrt{\dfrac{Qq}{\pi{ϵ}_{0}md^{3}}}

Hence, the~time period,~$T = $\dfrac{2\pi}{ω} =$2\$pi\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi{ϵ}_{0}md^{3}}{Qq}}

Therefore,~$T = \sqrt{\dfrac{4{π}^{3}{ε}_{0}ma^{3}}{{q}_{0}Q}}

$

questions.q: A simple pendulum of mass ' $m$ ', length ' $l$ ' and charge $' + q^{'}$ suspended in the electric field produced by two conducting parallel plates as shown. The value of deflection of pendulum in equilibrium position will be
questions.subject: Physics

Let $E$ be electric field in air

$Tsinθ = qE$

$tanθ = \dfrac{qE}{mg}$

$Q = \left[\dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1} + {C}_{2}}\right]\left[{V}_{1} + {V}_{2}\right]

$E = $\dfrac{Q}{A{Ïµ}_{o}} = \left[\dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1} + {C}_{2}}\right]\left[{V}_{1} + {V}_{2}\right]A{Ïµ}_{o}$

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{{Ïµ}_{0}A}{d - t} \toE = \dfrac{{C}_{2}\left[{V}_{1} + {V}_{2}\right]}{ \left({C}_{1} + {C}_{2}\right) ($d - t )}$

Now $θ = \tan^{- $1}\left[\dfrac{q · E}{mg}\right]

$θ = \tan^{- $1} \left[\dfrac{q}{mg}$× $\dfrac{{C}_{2} \left({V}_{1} + {V}_{2}\right)}{ \left({C}_{1} + {C}_{2}\right) ($d - t )}\right]

questions.q:
In free space, a particle $A$ of charge $1\muC$ is held fixed~at point $P$ . Another particle $B$ of the same charge and mass $4\mug$ is kept at a distance of $1$ mm from $P .$ If $B$ is released, then its velocity at a distance of $9$ mm from $P$ is:
[Take $\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{2}C^{- 2}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From conservation in mechanical energy:
$- \Delta P . E . = \Delta K . E .$
$\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\left(1 \times {10}^{6}\right)2\left[\dfrac{1}{10- 3} - \dfrac{1}{9 \times {10}^{- 3}}\right] = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times {10}^{- 6} \times V^{2}$
$9 \times {10}^{9} \times {10}^{- 12}\left[\dfrac{8}{9 \times {10}^{- 3}}\right] = 2 \times {10}^{- 6} \times V^{2}$
$V^{2} = 4 \times {10}^{6}$
$V = 2 \times {10}^{3}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A square loop of sides $a=1 \mathrm{~m}$ is held normally in front of a point charge $\mathrm{q}=1 \mathrm{C}$. The flux of the electric field through the shaded region is $\frac{5}{\mathrm{p}} \times \frac{1}{\varepsilon_0} \frac{\mathrm{Nm}^2}{\mathrm{C}}$, where the value of p is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Total flux through square $=\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\epsilon_0} $\$left(\frac{1}{6}\right) Lets divide square is 8 equal parts. Flux is same for each part. $\therefore$ Flux through shaded portion is \frac{5}{8} (Total flux) =\frac{5}{8} \times \frac{\mathrm{q}}{\epsilon_0} \frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{48} \frac{1}{\epsilon_0}\therefore required Ans. is 48

questions.q:
Two identical charged spheres are suspended by strings of equal lengths. The strings make an angle $\theta$ with each other. When suspended in water the angle remains the same. If density of the material of the sphere is $1 . 5g / cc,$ the dielectric constant of water will be ______.

(Take density of water $= 1g / cc$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In air:

$tan\dfrac{θ}{2} = \dfrac{F}{mg} = \dfrac{q2}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r^{2}mg}$

In water:

$tan\dfrac{θ}{2} = \dfrac{F '}{mg^{'}} = \dfrac{q2}{4\pi{ε}_{0}{ε}_{r}r^{2}{mg}_{eff}}$

Equate both equations, we get

${ε}_{0}g = {ε}_{0}{ε}_{r}g \left[$1 - $\dfrac{1}{1 . 5}\right]

$⇒ {ε}_{r} = 3$

$

questions.q: A thin infinite sheet charge and an infinite line charge of respective charge densities $+ \sigma$~and $+ \lambda$~are placed parallel at $5m$ distance from each~other. Points $P$ and $Q$ are at~$\dfrac{3}{π}m$ and~$\dfrac{4}{π}m$ perpendicular distances from line charge towards sheet charge, respectively.~${E}_{p}$~and~${E}_{q}$~are the magnitudes of resultant electric field intensities at point~$P$~and~$Q$~respectively. If~$\dfrac{EP}{EQ} = \dfrac{4}{a}$~for~$2 | \sigma | = | \lambda | ,$~then the value of~$a$& is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's consider the following diagram:

The formula to calculate the electric field due to an infinitely long charged sheet is given by

${E}_{s} = \dfrac{σ}{2{ε}_{0}} . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the electric field due to an infinitely long line charge is given by

${E}_{l} = $\dfrac{λ}{2\pi{ε}_{0}r} . . . \left(2\right)$

Using equations (1) and (2), the electric field at~$P$~can be calculated as follows:

\begin{cases}{E}_{P}$& = & \left|$\dfrac{σ}{2{ε}_{0}} - \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{2\lambda}{\dfrac{3}{π}}\right|$\\ & = & \left|$\dfrac{σ}{2{ε}_{0}} - \dfrac{λ}{6{ε}_{0}}\right|$\\ & = & $\dfrac{σ}{6{ε}_{0}} . . . \left($3\right)\end{cases}$

Similarly, the electric field at~$Q$~is given by

\begin{cases}{E}_{Q}$& = & \left|$\dfrac{σ}{2{ε}_{0}} - \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{2\lambda}{\dfrac{4}{π}}\right|$\\ & = & \left|$\dfrac{σ}{2{ε}_{0}} - \dfrac{λ}{8{ε}_{0}}\right|$\\ & = & $\dfrac{σ}{4{ε}_{0}} . . . \left($4\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (3) by equation (4) to obtain the required ratio.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{EP}{EQ}$& = & $\dfrac{\dfrac{σ}{6{ε}_{0}}}{\dfrac{σ}{4{ε}_{0}}}$\\ & = & $\dfrac{4}{6}$\\ & & \end{cases}$

Hence,~$a = 6$.

$

questions.q: $512$ identical drops of mercury are charged to a potential of $2V$ each. The drops are joined to form a single drop. The potential of this drop is $V$& in Volt.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: Three point charges of magnitude $5\muC, 0 . 16\muC$ and $0 . 3\muC$ are located at the vertices $A, B, C$ of a right angled triangle whose sides are $AB = 3cm$, $BC = 3\sqrt{2}cm$ and $CA = 3cm$ and point $A$ is the right angle corner. Charge at point $A$ experiences~_____~$N$& of electrostatic force due to the other two charges.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Coulomb's law the electrostatic force on& $A$~due to~$C$

${F}_{AC} = \dfrac{K{q}_{A}{q}_{C}}{\left({r}_{AC}\right)2} = \dfrac{k \times 5 \times 0 . 3 \times {10}^{- 12}}{9 \times {10}^{- 4}}= \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9} \times 5 \times 0 . 3 \times {10}^{- 12}}{9 \times {10}^{- 4}}$

$= 1 . 5 \times 10 = 15N$

Similarly, the force on~$A$~due to~$B$

${F}_{AB} = \dfrac{K{q}_{A}{q}_{B}}{\left({r}_{AB}\right)2} = \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{9} \times 5 \times 0 . 16 \times {10}^{- 12}}{9 \times {10}^{- 4}} = 8N$

We can see that the forces are perpendicular to each other. Therefore, the net force experienced by charge at $A$~is,

$F = \sqrt{{FAC}^{2} + {FAB}^{2}}= \sqrt{{15}^{2} + {8}^{2}} = \sqrt{289} = 17N$
